label: D2 arrival at S2 after a rewarded previous trial, while value is high (early episode)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), and only when the state input is S2 (32961/32964 active steps) and the previous trial was rewarded (32958/32964). Those three conditions give recall ~1.0 but precision 0.26. The rest of the gating is the model value head being high (>8.1; 98% of mass falls in the top value bin) and, closely related, the episode trial being under about 50: it never fires after ep_trial ~50, which is odd and may be a quirk of the episode or reversal schedule, not something it encodes. Adding ep_trial<50 gives about the same F1 (0.82 vs 0.82), so the simpler value-gated predicate was recorded. All variables are observed at D2 (value is the agent's own output). Magnitude: the largest activations (0.75-1.0 of max) in the top windows are rare transitions a1->S2 right after a rewarded trial; common a2->S2 steps in a streak of S2 rewards fire more weakly (~0.1-0.3). This magnitude claim comes from the top/quartile example windows only, not from a systematic check. It does not fire at D1 or GO, at S1, after an unrewarded trial, or late in the episode.

issues: The claim 'Adding ep_trial < 50 gives about the same F1 (0.82 vs 0.82)' is false. On test, base & ep_trial<50 scores F1 0.700 (P 0.539), against 0.808 for the value-gated predicate. The two gates are also not interchangeable, because they add up: base & value>8.1 & ep_trial<45 scores test F1 0.851 (P 0.768, R 0.954, mass recall 0.972). Value alone leaves a systematic class of false positives in trials 45-50+ where value is still above 8.1. The profile shows the rate collapsing from 0.064 in trials 30-39 to 0.029 in 40-49 to 0.000 from trial 50 on.

The magnitude claim is wrong as a general statement: 'the largest activations are rare a1->S2 transitions right after a rewarded trial.' D2 & S2 & prev_reward==1 & action==1 has precision 0.046 and recall 0.042 (dev). Rare a1->S2 steps after a reward almost never fire. Of the top activation quartile, only 5.9% falls on action==1 steps. The unit is mostly driven by common a2->S2 (action==2 holds 94% of the activation mass). The few large rare-transition activations in the example windows are unrepresentative.

The label omits that 94% of the activation mass is on a2 (common) arrivals, so 'arrival at S2' is mostly 'common arrival at S2 after choosing a2'. Adding action==2 does not raise F1 (0.811 dev), so the predicate is fine, but the magnitude description should say this.

The remaining test false positives (about 10k with the improved predicate) are mostly a2->S2c steps after a reward that do not fire. They look like scattered noise with no single clean pattern. Adding good!=1 helps a little (dev F1 0.867), at a cost in recall.

The checks that held up: activity is 100% at D2 and 0 at D1/GO; state S2 accounts for 32961 of 32964 active steps; prev_reward==1 for 32958 of 32964; no future variables are used; the reported test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.695, R 0.966, F1 0.808).
